title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 5 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

questions.prompt: What number does the colour red represent in the resistor colour code?
Two 60 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
The resistance of an LDR…
A diode allows current to flow in both directions.
Name the three legs of a transistor.
How can you tell which leg of an LED is positive?
questions.memo:
✓ The longer leg is the anode (+) (1)
✓ The shorter leg next to the flat edge is the cathode (−) (1)

questions.prompt: Which component would be the input sensor in an automatic night light?
Which component acts as an electronic switch in the process stage of many simple circuits?
A 12 V supply is across a 3 kΩ and a 1 kΩ resistor in series. What is the voltage across the 3 kΩ resistor?
A breadboard lets you test a circuit without soldering.
Classify each part of a fire alarm.
Give TWO safety precautions when soldering.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): ventilated area; use the stand; safety glasses; do not touch the tip; keep the cord away from the hot tip; wash hands after handling solder

questions.prompt: Iron rusts when it is in contact with:
questions.explanation: Rusting needs both oxygen and water. Remove either one and it stops.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical name for rust?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron oxide, formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

questions.prompt: Aluminium window frames rust if they are not painted.
questions.explanation: Aluminium is non-ferrous, so it cannot rust. It forms a thin protective oxide layer.

questions.prompt: Match each product with the most suitable preservation method.
Match each heat treatment with what it does.

pairs.right: Heat, then cool quickly; becomes hard but brittle
Reheat hardened steel; becomes tougher and less brittle
Heat, then cool very slowly; becomes soft and workable

questions.prompt: Give TWO ways in which preserving metals helps the environment, and ONE way in which a preservation process can harm it.
questions.memo:
✓ products last longer, so less metal has to be mined and processed (1)
✓ saves energy / less waste in landfills / fewer replacements (1)
✓ harm: e.g. toxic chemicals from electroplating or galvanising pollute water; paint solvents pollute the air (1)

questions.prompt: Biltong is preserved mainly by…
Freezing kills all micro-organisms in food.
questions.explanation: Freezing stops their growth; they can become active again when the food thaws.
